Figure 1:Overview of EgoX.EgoX learns from highly diverse embodiments, including humans, a humanoid,
a wheeled bimanual robot, a quadruped, tabletop arms, and a simulated humanoid, with dexterous
hands, grippers, and tools as end-effectors. It first pretrains on egocentric cross-embodiment data
from humans and robots (top left), then fine-tunes on a new embodiment–task domain (bottom left). Its model, MXT+, routes each embodiment’s observations through
modality tokenizers into a shared Transformer trunk and decodes actions with embodiment-specific action
experts, while a training-only dreaming expert predicts future embodiment latents (center). The
resulting policies perform manipulation across embodiments and long-horizon loco-manipulation on a
humanoid (right, top and middle). Embodiment dreaming and cross-embodiment pretraining both improve
the average task progress score and success rate (right, bottom).
